_doc: SKEPTIC (c): pulse-phase decomposition of the topped rail's dV/dt. Computed on the PRIOR ANALYSIS's own decks so this conclusion does not depend on my re-run.

FINDINGS.delivery_vs_delivery: clamp 58.5 V/ns during conduction vs pulsed 10.5 V/ns during freewheel = 5.6x gentler. The brief's mechanism claim is CORRECT AT THE DELIVERY PHASE -- a series inductor really does ramp the rail.
FINDINGS.but_the_dominant_edge_is_elsewhere: in BOTH forms the largest edge is the top-up switch's TURN-OFF: clamp 227.0 V/ns, pulsed 92.0 V/ns. That is 2.47x, not the order of magnitude the brief's 'no voltage discontinuity' implies.
FINDINGS.the_prior_mechanism_is_REFUTED: the prior analysis attributed the pulsed form's 92 V/ns to the stored inductor current dumping in as the OUT switch CLOSES. MEASURED: at OUT-close the slope is 0.125 V/ns, and at the OUT-OPEN edge I(LTU3) = 0.36 uA. The inductor is empty when the big edge happens. It is gate-drive feedthrough at turn-off.
FINDINGS.ZCS_is_actually_good: I(LTU3) ramps 818 -> 1169 uA across the pulse and returns to 0.36 uA at the cut. The freewheel timing is correct; the inductor is doing its job. The residual step is not its fault -- it belongs to the isolation switch that AMENDMENT A1b proved mandatory.
FINDINGS.verdict: step coupling is REDUCED, NOT ELIMINATED, and the residual is STRUCTURAL.
